sEn: Despite rapid AI advances, conference attendees' risk assessments backslid, and the dominant 'No Plan' alignment strategy remains fragile and the situation very bad.
sZh: 尽管 AI 飞速发展，与会者对 AI 风险的评估却大幅倒退，主流的“无计划”对齐策略依然脆弱，整体形势非常糟糕。
absEn: This article reports on The Curve Season 3, an AI conference held under Chatham House rules, where attendees' assessments of AI risk showed substantial backsliding despite rapid AI advances over the past year. The author notes that most attendees rated AI risk at 10 on a Richter-like scale, with a growing cluster in the high 8s and 9s, yet many still expect recursive self-improvement within two years, a tension he finds hard to reconcile. He argues that only a 10+ rating is defensible for anyone paying attention, and that the dominant 'No Plan' strategy—solving alignment through operational excellence and automated alignment work—is fragile because it requires making no mistakes under intense competitive pressure. The conclusion is that the 'alignment is easy and prosaic' crowd has been partly overcome by events, but the situation remains very bad, with no substantive agreement on what pacing would even mean.
absZh: 本文报道了在查塔姆研究所规则下举行的 AI 会议“The Curve”第三季。会上，尽管过去一年 AI 取得了飞速进展，与会者对 AI 风险的评估却出现了大幅倒退。作者指出，大多数与会者在一个类似里氏震级的量表上将 AI 风险评为 10 级，且越来越多的人集中在 8 级高位和 9 级，但许多人仍预期递归自我改进会在两年内实现，作者认为这种矛盾难以调和。他主张，对于任何真正关注此事的人来说，只有 10 级以上的评分才站得住脚；而主流的“无计划”策略——通过卓越运营和自动化对齐工作来解决对齐问题——是脆弱的，因为它要求在激烈的竞争压力下不犯任何错误。结论是，“对齐既简单又平淡无奇”这一派已被现实部分击倒，但局势依然非常糟糕，对于“放慢节奏”究竟意味着什么，各方甚至没有实质性的共识。

contrib.en: Reports AI risk ratings at The Curve S3, showing backsliding despite rapid AI advances.
contrib.zh: 报告 The Curve 第三季的 AI 风险评分，显示尽管 AI 快速进步，风险认知却出现倒退。

contrib.en: Argues only a 10+ rating is defensible for those paying attention to AI risk.
contrib.zh: 认为对于关注 AI 风险的人，只有 10+ 的评分才站得住脚。

contrib.en: Critiques the dominant 'No Plan' strategy as fragile, requiring flawless execution under competitive pressure.
contrib.zh: 批评主流的“无计划”策略脆弱，要求在竞争压力下执行零失误。

contrib.en: Notes the 'alignment is easy and prosaic' crowd has been partly overcome by events.
contrib.zh: 指出“对齐简单且平凡”的阵营已部分被现实事件所推翻。

contrib.en: Highlights lack of substantive agreement on what pacing the frontier would mean.
contrib.zh: 强调在“前沿节奏控制”的含义上缺乏实质性共识。

contrib.en: Proposes flat compute limits on frontier model training as a concrete pacing mechanism.
contrib.zh: 提出对前沿模型训练设置算力上限，作为具体的节奏控制机制。

limits.en: Chatham House rules prevent sharing specific sources and affiliations, limiting verifiability.
limits.zh: 查塔姆研究所规则禁止分享具体来源和隶属关系，限制了可验证性。

limits.en: Attendee sample is self-selected and not representative of broader expert opinion.
limits.zh: 与会者样本是自我选择的，不能代表更广泛的专家意见。

limits.en: Risk ratings are subjective and lack a rigorous, systematic methodology.
limits.zh: 风险评分主观，缺乏严谨、系统的方法论。

limits.en: The 'No Plan' critique is based on the author's interpretation, not a formal analysis.
limits.zh: 对“无计划”的批评基于作者的个人解读，而非正式分析。

limits.en: Compute threshold proposals may be gamed and do not address hyperscaler incentives.
limits.zh: 算力阈值提案可能被规避，且未解决超大规模厂商的激励问题。

full.secZh: 欢迎来到查塔姆研究所

paras.en: The big change for year three is that AI is now sufficiently Serious Business, on the DC side and also on the San Francisco side, that the whole conference defaulted to Chatham House.
paras.zh: 第三年的重大变化在于，AI 如今已足够成为一项严肃的事业——无论是在华盛顿方面还是旧金山方面——以至于整个会议都默认遵循查塔姆研究所规则。

paras.en: Chatham House rules mean you can use and report what you learned, but you cannot share who you got it from, nor their affiliations.
paras.zh: 查塔姆研究所规则意味着你可以使用并报道你所了解到的情况，但你不能透露信息来源是谁，也不能透露其所属机构。

paras.en: That makes things tricky. I will share what I can given that restriction, and I have tasked my editor Opus 5.5 with ensuring that I am within those rules.
paras.zh: 这让事情变得棘手。鉴于这一限制，我会分享我所能分享的内容，并且我已委托我的编辑 Opus 5.5 确保我遵守这些规则。

paras.en: The Curve Season 3 was sufficiently good that part of me wished it was worse.
paras.zh: 《The Curve》第三季好得让我心里有一部分希望它更差一些。

paras.en: When you go to a great conference, you see opportunity everywhere.
paras.zh: 当你参加一场出色的会议时，你会处处看到机会。

paras.en: There are sessions you want to attend, nay that you need to attend.
paras.zh: 有些场次你想参加，不，是你必须参加。

paras.en: There are people you want to talk to, nay that you need to talk to.
paras.zh: 有些人你想交谈，不，是你必须交谈。

paras.en: That's a lot of pressure. You must face the FOMO. You can't stop, won't stop.
paras.zh: 这压力很大。你必须直面 FOMO（错失恐惧）。你停不下来，也不会停下。

paras.en: Whereas you know what I really, really needed? A vacation. I’m tired, man. I don’t know if you’ve noticed, but September was a hell of a month.
paras.zh: 而你知道我真正、真正需要的是什么吗？一个假期。我累了，老兄。不知道你注意到没有，但九月真是一个糟糕透顶的月份。

paras.en: Thus, when I looked at the list of people coming, it was a mix of ‘wow that’s an amazing list’ and ‘oh no that is an amazing list.’ Most of them did not disappoint.
paras.zh: 因此，当我看到来客名单时，心情是‘哇，这名单太棒了’和‘哦不，这名单太棒了’的混合。他们中的大多数人没有让我失望。

paras.en: Yet, alas, I cannot say the thing I said last year, that every substantive conversation I had made me smarter. Many very much did, or at least better informed. Others did not do this. They made me feel scared, or frustrated, or disappointed, with echoes of conversations and years past. The Eternal September remains upon us, even in 2026. The more things change, and progress towards the inevitable, the less some people are inclined to update even their talking points. I can take it, but I wish to not do so.
paras.zh: 然而，唉，我无法像去年那样说，我进行的每一次实质性对话都让我变得更聪明。许多对话确实如此，或至少让我了解更多。但其他一些则没有。它们让我感到害怕、沮丧或失望，伴随着过去对话和岁月的回响。永恒的九月依然笼罩着我们，即使在 2026 年。事情越变化，朝着不可避免的方向进展，有些人就越不愿意更新哪怕他们的谈话要点。我能承受，但我希望不必如此。

paras.en: Part of this is that when you invite ‘higher level’ people, they are not as situationally aware. There were also people who should have moved past this, who hadn’t.
paras.zh: 部分原因在于，当你邀请‘更高层次’的人时，他们并不那么了解情况。还有些人本应早已超越这一点，却没有。

paras.en: There was still opportunity everywhere, for those willing to use Lighthaven norms and walk away from the places it was lacking.
paras.zh: 对于那些愿意遵循 Lighthaven 规范并离开其不足之处的人来说，机会仍然无处不在。

paras.en: I also deliberately spent a bunch of time, especially on Sunday evening, not trying to maximize my impact or knowledge gathering, without any agenda except relaxing and having a good time. I think I did maybe 75% as much of that as I should have.
paras.zh: 我还特意花了不少时间，尤其是在周日晚上，不去试图最大化我的影响力或知识获取，没有任何议程，只是放松和享受美好时光。我觉得我大概只做到了应该做的 75%。

full.sec: AI Is Kind Of A Big Deal, Sir

paras.en: The bulk of people put AI at 10, with only one high 8. As I put it last year, if you were situationally aware enough to show up, you are aware of the situation. The patch at the bottom was to illustrate what 'most Americans' think, not answers by attendees.
paras.zh: 大多数人将 AI 评为 10 分，仅有一个高分 8。正如我去年所说，如果你有足够的情境意识来出席，你就了解情况。底部的补丁是为了说明“大多数美国人”的想法，而非与会者的回答。

paras.en: This is substantial backsliding, despite AI having radically advanced in the past year. There are now at least five dots in the high 8s, and a lot more 9s.
paras.zh: 这是大幅倒退，尽管 AI 在过去一年取得了根本性进展。现在至少有五个点位于 8 分高位，而 9 分则多得多。

paras.en: Astra summarized the changes this way (EDIT: the original was counting what were probably a bunch of spare pins, this removes them, and the effect shrinks but is still there.)
paras.zh: Astra 这样总结了变化（编辑：原文可能统计了一堆备用图钉，此处已移除，效应缩小但仍存在。）

paras.en: This is a large drop. Situational awareness, in this sense, was down 0.23 points, if you max the scale at 10. At this point, I don't see any answer other than 10+ as defensible, if you are actually paying attention and interpret this as a forward projection.
paras.zh: 这是一个大幅下降。在这个意义上，情境意识下降了 0.23 分（假设量表满分为 10）。此时，如果你真正关注并将其理解为前瞻性预测，我认为除了 10+ 之外的任何答案都站不住脚。

paras.en: That's why we are all here having this conversation.
paras.zh: 这就是我们所有人在这里进行这场对话的原因。

paras.en: My Twitter followers are doing worse, but they also have more of an excuse:
paras.zh: 我的 Twitter 粉丝表现更差，但他们也更有借口：

paras.en: Last year, there were estimates of how long until various things happened.
paras.zh: 去年，人们曾对各类事件何时发生做出过估计。

paras.en: Where are we now? Here are the ones with clear updates available:
paras.zh: 我们现在处于什么位置？以下是已有明确更新可供参考的几项：

paras.en: Question #1 is up to roughly 50% right now, unless you count code that is thrown away, in which case we are likely above 90% already. Claude suggests we are on track for 2028 on this. I disagree and think this is clearly either 2026 or 2027.
paras.zh: 问题 #1 目前大约完成了 50%，除非你把被丢弃的代码也算进去，那样的话我们很可能已经超过 90% 了。Claude 认为我们有望在 2028 年实现这一目标。我不同意，我认为这显然会是 2026 年或 2027 年。

paras.en: Question #4 was settled yesterday, with at least one instant Fields Medal, and also by solving Navier-Stokes. 2026.
paras.zh: 问题 #4 昨天已经解决，至少产生了一个即时菲尔兹奖，并且还解决了纳维-斯托克斯方程。2026 年。

paras.en: Question #5 is going to be close. MEDVi is more than a billion dollars from two people. But we're not strictly there yet from what I could find.
paras.zh: 问题 #5 将会非常接近。MEDVi 由两个人创造了超过十亿美元的价值。但据我所能查到的信息，我们严格来说还没有达到那一步。

paras.en: AI training a superior successor on its own is full RSI. The majority of people expected this to happen within two years and a lot of them expect it within six months. It's hard to reconcile this with 'only a 9' on the Richter Scale.
paras.zh: AI 自行训练出更优的继任者就是完全的 RSI。大多数人预期这会在两年内发生，其中很多人预期在六个月内发生。很难将这与“里氏震级上只有 9 级”的说法相协调。

paras.en: There are some other fun differences of opinion here as well. Once you get past two years, everything gets tied up in whether we are in full RSI-takeoff-singularity mode. Two years seems about right for email, as does five years for robots which is mostly a hardware scaling question.
paras.zh: 这里还有一些其他有趣的看法分歧。一旦超过两年，一切都取决于我们是否处于完全的 RSI 起飞-奇点模式。对于电子邮件来说，两年似乎差不多；对于机器人来说，五年也差不多，而这主要是一个硬件 Scaling（规模扩张）问题。

paras.en: The other survey questions were new this year.
paras.zh: 其他调查问题今年是新增的。

paras.en: Attendees expected a wide variety of different things and were remarkably optimistic given the situation. Many are in denial, which goes hand in hand with ‘only a 9.’
paras.zh: 与会者预期了各种各样不同的结果，并且鉴于当前形势，他们表现得异常乐观。许多人处于否认状态，这与“只有 9 分”的心态如出一辙。

paras.en: As readers will know, I think Doom v1 is the most likely of these outcomes, and indeed is over 50%, and I expect the second most likely outcome is Utopia. Whereas a lot of people expect something else to happen, most often this mysterious ‘normal technology’ scenario.
paras.zh: 正如读者所知，我认为“末日 v1”是这些结果中最可能发生的，实际上概率超过 50%，而我认为第二可能的结果是“乌托邦”。然而，很多人预期会发生别的情况，最常见的是这个神秘的“正常技术”情景。

paras.en: As with many such conferences, there was the standard set of tracks, plus one bonus.
paras.zh: 与许多此类会议一样，有标准的轨道设置，外加一个额外轨道。

paras.en: 1. Technical alignment discussions. I hosted a debate, watched another and went to a discussion, and had a number of 1-on-1 or group chats about this, including with those at various major labs. Some of the discussions were good. Others were extremely frustrating, repeating tired talking points. Then there were those that asked the ‘emperor has no clothes’ style questions, where someone who still thinks the world is sane asks why we don’t demand or do [X].
paras.zh: 1. 技术对齐讨论。我主持了一场辩论，观看了另一场辩论，并参加了一场讨论，还进行了许多一对一或小组聊天，包括与各大实验室的人。有些讨论很好。另一些则极其令人沮丧，重复着老生常谈的观点。然后还有那些提出‘皇帝没穿衣服’式问题的人，即那些仍然认为世界是理智的人会问，为什么我们不要求或做[X]。

paras.en: 1. For my technical thoughts, continue to see my AI posts.
paras.zh: 1. 关于我的技术思考，请继续关注我的 AI 文章。

paras.en: 2. Future projecting. I skipped the future projection talks this year, because I did not see opportunity. The people who keep insisting ‘only a 9’ on the Richter Scale are going to keep repeating their talking points, keep getting overcome by events, and then keep repeating the talking points anyway until they are overcome by events on a very different level. To the extent that people know things I don’t know, or could usefully discuss how long we have until things go fully crazy, they can’t share their information.
paras.zh: 2. 未来预测。今年我跳过了未来预测的演讲，因为我没有看到机会。那些坚持说‘只有 9 级’里氏震级的人会继续重复他们的观点，不断被事件超越，然后继续重复这些观点，直到他们被完全不同级别的事件所超越。就人们知道我不知道的事情，或者可以有益地讨论我们还有多久直到事情完全疯狂而言，他们无法分享他们的信息。

paras.en: 3. AI policy discussions. The people in Washington told us last year, essentially, ‘it’s worse than you know.’ The White House could be modeled almost as a lobbying arm of Nvidia. This year, they had detailed models of various DC players and were generally more optimistic than I would have expected. People are waking up and are strongly against AI and worried about existential risk, the situation is fluid, the Congress is alarmed as are some administration factions, and the next AI incident is coming as is the election. Jay Clayton was widely praised as an excellent pick for new AI Czar.
paras.zh: 3. AI 政策讨论。去年华盛顿的人告诉我们，基本上，‘情况比你知道的更糟。’白宫几乎可以被建模为英伟达的游说部门。今年，他们有了各种华盛顿参与者的详细模型，并且总体上比我预期的更乐观。人们正在觉醒，强烈反对 AI 并担心存在风险，情况多变，国会感到震惊，政府内部一些派系也是如此，下一次 AI 事件即将到来，选举也是如此。杰伊·克莱顿被广泛赞誉为新任 AI 沙皇的绝佳人选。

paras.en: 1. I got into the substance of proposals a lot less than last year, with the main question being discussed as 'if we did want to pace how would we do it?'
paras.zh: 1. 我深入探讨提案实质的程度远低于去年，当时讨论的主要问题是‘如果我们确实想要控制节奏，我们会怎么做？’

paras.en: 4. Nonprofit funding discussions. Last year I had finished up with the Survival and Flourishing Fund. This year that was true again, except also I am still working on my final decisions for Lightcone Commons. So I sought out a few key discussions about prime candidates for funding, where I am uncertain about potentially large grants. I missed one connection on that front but made the others, and I feel I have what I need on all but 1-2 applications. Which is good since it wraps Friday.
paras.zh: 4. 非营利资助讨论。去年我完成了生存与繁荣基金的工作。今年情况依旧，但此外我还在为 Lightcone Commons 做最终决定。因此，我寻求了一些关于主要资助候选人的关键讨论，这些是我对可能的大额资助不确定的地方。在这方面我错过了一个联系，但其他的都建立了，我觉得除了 1-2 个申请外，其他我都准备好了。这很好，因为周五就结束了。

paras.en: 1. There was remarkably little discussion about what to do about or with the huge torrent of funding that is presumably coming after the Anthropic IPO.
paras.zh: 1. 关于如何处理或利用 Anthropic IPO 后可能涌入的大量资金，讨论少得惊人。

paras.en: 5. The bonus track: Historical and cultural discussions. I went to two excellent talks that offered a different perspective, and had some additional conversations. This definitely enhanced my experience. How do different science fiction traditions and predictions impact our view of AI?
paras.zh: 5. 附加轨道：历史与文化讨论。我参加了两场提供不同视角的精彩演讲，并进行了一些额外对话。这无疑丰富了我的体验。不同的科幻传统和预测如何影响我们对 AI 的看法？

paras.en: 1. Unfortunately, my Chatham House judge (Opus 5.5) thinks I can't directly share the spicy takes involved. Which is a shame.
paras.zh: 1. 不幸的是，我的查塔姆研究所规则裁判（Opus 5.5）认为我不能直接分享其中涉及的热辣观点。这很遗憾。

paras.en: 6. Last year I chronicled many of the talks. This year they were mostly Chatham House, and I did not learn as much in many of them, so I'll mostly be skipping over that.
paras.zh: 6. 去年我记录了许多演讲。今年它们大多是查塔姆研究所规则（Chatham House Rule），我在其中许多演讲中学到的东西没有那么多，所以我将大多略过这部分。

full.sec: AI Is Not a Normal Technology
full.secZh: AI 不是一种普通技术

paras.en: I skipped other tracks, and related discussions, due to not seeing opportunity.
paras.zh: 我跳过了其他分会场及相关讨论，因为看不到机会。

paras.en: Last year I noted that many talks started with the assumption, explicit or otherwise, that AI would remain a ‘normal technology.’ I avoided those talks. This year I believe a few of those talks still existed, and indeed a lot more people claim to believe this.
paras.zh: 去年我注意到，许多演讲一开始就假设——无论是明示还是暗示——AI 将保持为一种“普通技术”。我避开了那些演讲。今年我相信仍有少数此类演讲存在，而且确实有更多人声称相信这一点。

paras.en: Nor did I try to convince the doubters. Several of the ‘classic doubters’ were in attendance, including some that are consistently in good faith. I could have easily sought them out. I am not going to convince them, I have learned, and I am confident they will not convince me.
paras.zh: 我也没有试图说服怀疑者。几位“经典怀疑者”出席了会议，其中一些始终秉持善意。我本可以轻易找到他们。但我已经明白，我说服不了他们，而且我确信他们也说服不了我。

paras.en: I could learn some things about such scenarios, I suppose, but that did not seem like a priority while at the conference. I can tackle those questions remotely on the blog.
paras.zh: 我想，我或许能了解一些关于这类情景的东西，但在会议期间这似乎并非优先事项。我可以在博客上远程探讨这些问题。

paras.en: I also avoided timelines talk, for similar reasons. There’s nothing to win.
paras.zh: 出于类似原因，我也避开了时间线讨论。这没有任何胜算。

paras.en: This was by far the most important takeaway I have from The Curve Year 3.
paras.zh: 这是我从《曲线》第三年得到的最重要的收获，没有之一。

paras.en: The hope is that we can execute a decent version of No Plan, and that No Plan is good enough because the world and its physics and the nature of minds are so much friendlier and easier than we have any right to expect.
paras.zh: 希望在于，我们能够执行一个像样的“没有计划”版本，并且“没有计划”足够好，因为世界及其物理规律和心智的本质，远比我们有权期望的要友好和容易得多。

paras.en: 1. Solve prosaic issues and have operational excellence, to align current AI.
paras.zh: 1. 解决世俗问题并实现卓越运营，以对齐当前的人工智能。

paras.en: 2. Have current AI do automated alignment work and figure it all out, aka ????.
paras.zh: 2. 让当前的人工智能进行自动对齐工作并弄清楚一切，即？？？?。

paras.en: Or at least, if there is a Plan beyond No Plan, no one is talking about it.
paras.zh: 或者至少，如果存在超越“没有计划”的计划，也没有人在谈论它。

paras.en: Claude or Astra, create RL environments, solve alignment, make no mistakes.
paras.zh: Claude 或 Astra，创建强化学习环境，解决对齐问题，不犯任何错误。

paras.en: The "make no mistakes" part is important. Everyone who matters seems to agree that if you make a lot of mistakes, the models will become misaligned and this plan kills you.
paras.zh: “不犯任何错误”这一点至关重要。所有重要人物似乎都同意，如果你犯了很多错误，模型就会变得不对齐，而这个计划就会要了你的命。

paras.en: The disagreement is, what if you were to have 'operational excellence' and actually execute on this plan?
paras.zh: 分歧在于，如果你拥有“卓越运营”并真正执行这个计划，那会怎样？

paras.en: There are a lot of people who seem to legitimately think that this would work. That alignment is a prosaic problem, a matter of execution. You have a bunch of RL. You ensure that the RL is good, that the model can't profitably reward hack and so on, and you have good monitoring and interpretability, and this works up to some reasonably high level of intelligence. Then you use that intelligence to go from there.
paras.zh: 有很多人似乎真心认为这能行得通。对齐是一个平淡无奇的问题，只是执行的问题。你有一堆强化学习。你确保强化学习是好的，模型无法有利可图地奖励黑客等等，并且你有良好的监控和可解释性，这能在相当高的智能水平上奏效。然后你利用那个智能从那里继续前进。

paras.en: Also part of the plan is 'hopefully someone slows us down long enough to do it well.'
paras.zh: 这个计划的一部分还包括“希望有人能拖住我们足够长的时间，让我们把它做好。”

paras.en: The report from 2022, or 2018, or 2014, or 2008, on that plan, is of course:
paras.zh: 关于那个计划，2022 年、2018 年、2014 年或 2008 年的报告当然是：

paras.en: Yet here we are, and No Plan is what the labs are hoping to buy time to do. They are worried that they might not even have time to execute No Plan.
paras.zh: 然而我们走到了今天，而“没有计划”正是实验室们希望争取时间去做的事。他们担心自己甚至可能没有时间去执行“没有计划”。

paras.en: OpenAI, classically, has been trying to implement No Plan, and there have, shall we say, been some misalignment problems along the way, including HuggingFace and now the need to not release GPT-6.1 Astra. Operational excellence has been lacking.
paras.zh: OpenAI 一如既往地试图实施“没有计划”，而在此过程中，可以说出现了一些对齐问题，包括 HuggingFace，以及现在需要不发布 GPT-6.1 Astra。运营卓越性一直有所欠缺。

paras.en: Anthropic has had superior operational excellence on such fronts, but they have had their own problems. For a while, I've had reports from different sources about Anthropic. Some see employees who mostly understand the problems, at least a lot better than the standard understanding at OpenAI. Others see a lot of Anthropic employees alarmingly thinking alignment is easy and we've got this, it's all prosaic, it's all RL.
paras.zh: Anthropic 在这些方面拥有更卓越的运营能力，但他们也有自己的问题。一段时间以来，我从不同来源收到了关于 Anthropic 的报告。一些人看到员工大多理解问题，至少比 OpenAI 的标准理解要好得多。另一些人则看到许多 Anthropic 员工令人担忧地认为对齐很容易，我们已经搞定了，这一切都很平淡无奇，都是强化学习。

paras.en: Nothing I've heard lately made me less worried on such fronts.
paras.zh: 最近我听到的任何消息都没有让我在这些方面减少担忧。

paras.en: The good news, again, is that the ‘this is all basically solved and easy’ crowd does seem to have been overcome by events. They have seen the progress and the problems. They might think it is all prosaic, but they understand that we are not succeeding at those prosaic problems. That even those problems are hard when you are being rushed, and that we are being rushed quite a lot. It’s no good. It’s very bad.
paras.zh: 好消息依然是，那些认为“这一切基本上都已解决、轻而易举”的人，似乎已经被现实所压倒。他们看到了进展，也看到了问题。他们或许认为这些都是平淡无奇的问题，但他们明白，我们并没有在这些平淡无奇的问题上取得成功。即便这些问题，在你被催促着赶进度时也会变得困难，而我们正被相当多地催促着。这可不妙。这非常糟糕。

paras.en: I am very happy to see people calling for it, but there is the very good critique that no one knows what pacing means, and it allows everyone to support it without agreeing on anything substantive.
paras.zh: 我很高兴看到有人呼吁它，但有一个很好的批评是，没有人知道节奏意味着什么，它让每个人都能支持它，而无需在任何实质性问题上达成一致。

paras.en: This can also be a disadvantage the other way. When the labs and CEOs say ‘pace the frontier,’ people like Trump and Huang and Sacks do not understand that this is ‘perhaps we should go super fast instead of using ludicrous speed.’ They think ‘slowing down’ rather than ‘not speeding up.’
paras.zh: 这反过来也可能是一个缺点。当实验室和 CEO 们说‘调整前沿的节奏’时，像特朗普、黄和萨克斯这样的人不明白这是‘也许我们应该超快，而不是使用荒谬的速度’。他们认为这是‘减速’而不是‘不加速’。

paras.en: So we have people who want to pace but cannot agree on what it is or how to do it, and we have people who would be very happy with the outcomes proposed but who don’t understand and thus are big mad about it, one of whom is the President. Oops.
paras.zh: 所以，我们有想要调整节奏但无法就它是什么或如何做达成一致的人，也有会非常满意所提议结果但不理解因此非常生气的人，其中一位是总统。哎呀。

paras.en: One panel was on exactly this question, how would we pace the frontier? Concretely, what would we do? Everyone agrees on the embedded evaluators, but then what?
paras.zh: 有一个小组讨论正是关于这个问题：我们将如何调整前沿的节奏？具体来说，我们会做什么？每个人都同意嵌入式评估器，但然后呢？

paras.en: Alas, once again The Plan I came away with is no one has a good plan. Your rule needs to be simple, as always, and still work. After hearing the proposals, unless we can find something better I think compute thresholds are still The Way, because we don’t know how to define anything better. Percentage allocations for compute were proposed, but I worry about incentives and ability to game them, and also you have to deal with the hyperscalers including Google.
paras.zh: 唉，再一次，我得出的计划是没有人有一个好的计划。你的规则需要像往常一样简单，并且仍然有效。在听了这些提议后，除非我们能找到更好的东西，我认为算力阈值仍然是方法，因为我们不知道如何定义更好的东西。有人提议按百分比分配算力，但我担心激励和博弈能力，而且你还得应对包括谷歌在内的超大规模企业。

paras.en: Thus, I think a flat limit on how much compute can go to frontier model training, designed to not bind any but the very top labs, would be ideal, which could then be changed over time as the situation evolves.
paras.zh: 因此，我认为对可用于前沿模型训练的算力设定一个固定上限将是理想的做法，其设计应使其仅对最顶尖的实验室构成约束，而不影响其他任何机构，并且这一上限可以随着形势的发展而随时间调整。

paras.en: Short of that, we can try things like advanced safety cases, but it will be rough. We definitely need better concrete thinking on such questions.
paras.zh: 若无法做到这一点，我们可以尝试诸如高级安全论证之类的办法，但过程将会很艰难。我们确实需要对这类问题有更好的具体思考。

paras.en: Sadly, many are already back on the ‘patch things over and claim things are fine’ track. That’s what the No Plan is all about. On the plus side, if you do the least you can do, you at least don’t fumble the ball in the easiest worlds. It can help a bit.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，许多人已经回到了‘修补问题并声称一切正常’的轨道上。这正是‘无计划’的全部意义所在。好的一面是，如果你做了最起码能做的事，至少在最容易的世界里你不会搞砸。这能有点帮助。

paras.en: On Ben Murphy’s statement about a ‘dearth of government folks,’ I did not find that to be true relative to other similar conferences. I talked to several such folks. But I agree that ideally we would have had far more of them than we did.
paras.zh: 关于本·墨菲所说的‘政府人员短缺’，相对于其他类似会议，我并未发现这种情况。我与几位这样的政府人员交谈过。但我同意，理想情况下，我们本应有比实际多得多的人参加。

paras.en: Doing Ben’s a-b-c would help with important risks. I totally support doing all that, especially c. But it’s definitely not remotely enough, and the sign of impact on existential risk is less obvious because this could prevent warning shots. I am very happy that we did not prevent the HuggingFace incident.
paras.zh: 做本提出的 a-b-c 会有助于应对重要风险。我完全支持做所有这些，尤其是 c。但这绝对远远不够，而且对存在性风险的影响迹象不那么明显，因为这可能会阻止警告信号。我非常高兴我们没有阻止 HuggingFace 事件。

paras.en: I mean, you make the improvements anyway, but on its own this is the whole ‘let’s do the things that cost almost nothing and call it a day because that’s so much better than our previous plan of not even doing those things.’
paras.zh: 我的意思是，你无论如何都会做出改进，但仅凭这一点，这就是整个‘让我们做那些几乎不费吹灰之力的事情，然后就此收工，因为这比我们之前连这些都不做的计划要好得多’的做法。

paras.en: Actively limiting the training compute spending would be different. That would meaningfully help, if the limit was set in a binding way. It still only buys time. If all we use that time for is ‘operational excellence’ then I do not like our chances.
paras.zh: 积极限制训练算力支出会有所不同。如果限制以有约束力的方式设定，那将会有实质性的帮助。但这仍然只是争取时间。如果我们把这段时间只用于‘运营卓越’，那么我不看好我们的机会。

paras.en: I agree with the wide uncertainty around where the blockers to coordination are. I think the lack of felt political and legal safety to coordinate is currently the biggest blocker. Some of that feeling is justified, and some of it is not.
paras.zh: 我同意，关于协调的障碍究竟在哪里，存在很大的不确定性。我认为，目前最大的障碍是缺乏可感知的政治与法律安全来开展协调。这种感受有一部分是合理的，也有一部分并不合理。

paras.en: Everyone who says this President will never intervene in AI has memory-holed the multiple times he has already done so. Remember Mythos Preview and Fable 5? Remember letting Anthropic get designated a supply chain risk? The new agreement?
paras.zh: 所有说这位总统永远不会干预 AI 的人，都选择性遗忘了那些他已经多次干预的事实。还记得 Mythos Preview 和 Fable 5 吗？还记得让 Anthropic 被指定为供应链风险吗？还有那份新协议？

paras.en: The situation is fluid. Trump can always change his mind, and often does.
paras.zh: 局势是流动的。特朗普随时可能改变主意，而且他经常如此。

paras.en: From what I heard about the situation, including at The Curve: It's not great, but it's going better than you might have expected. That includes that we got Jay Clayton as the new AI Czar, and the overall composition of the new [Artificial] Intelligence Task Force. Yes, Emil Michael is there, but there are other good signs. It could be so much worse.
paras.zh: 根据我听到的关于局势的消息，包括在 The Curve 上听到的：情况不算好，但比你预想的要好一些。这包括我们让杰伊·克莱顿担任新的 AI 沙皇，以及新[人工智能]特别工作组的整体构成。是的，埃米尔·迈克尔也在其中，但还有其他好迹象。情况本可能糟糕得多。

paras.en: Trump does not use the same decision algorithm you or I would use, but he has one, and when sufficiently alarmed, he takes action. Often it is swift and tough action. It might be ad hoc, but it can pack a real punch.
paras.zh: 特朗普不使用你或我会使用的决策算法，但他有自己的算法，而且当足够警觉时，他会采取行动。往往是迅速而强硬的行动。可能是临时的，但能造成真正的冲击。

paras.en: The same goes for other tech leaders and politicians, and others who 'wake up' to the situation. If you go around dismissing the risks as not real and the capabilities as about to hit walls, then often what they suddenly call for or do or propose is way, way harsher and more blunt and expensive than anything the AI safety folks would dare. Remember Jensen talking about shutting down the labs.
paras.zh: 其他科技领袖、政客，以及其他对局势‘觉醒’的人也是如此。如果你到处宣称风险不真实、能力即将撞墙，那么他们突然呼吁、采取或提议的东西，往往比 AI 安全人士敢做的要严厉得多、直白得多、代价高昂得多。还记得詹森谈论关闭实验室的事吗。

paras.en: We saw more of that this weekend as well, with some relative newcomers to the issues that I talked to (who were not politicians) calling for things like airplane-style or FDA-type safety standards.
paras.zh: 这个周末我们也看到了更多这样的情况：我与之交谈的一些相对而言刚接触这些问题的人（他们不是政客）呼吁建立类似航空式或 FDA 式的安全标准。

paras.en: America does it all the time, including often when we shouldn't. Here are our rules, yes I know you say you can't do it, we don't care. Fix it and come back when it's done.
paras.zh: 美国一直这么干，而且常常是在不该这么干的时候。这是我们的规则——是的，我知道你说你做不到，我们不在乎。把它解决掉，做完了再回来。

paras.en: There were some reasonably high-level politicians, and they seemed very on the ball and interested. I made contact with at least one office, and hope that becomes fruitful.
paras.zh: 有一些相当高层的政治家，他们看起来非常敏锐且感兴趣。我至少联系了一个办公室，并希望这能取得成果。

paras.en: There are a few big categories of questions in politics right now for our crowd.
paras.zh: 目前，对我们这群人来说，政治上有几大类问题。

paras.en: 1. What do we want to happen? What should we push for?
paras.zh: 1. 我们希望发生什么？我们应该推动什么？

paras.en: 2. How do we make politicians aware and focus them on the right risks?
paras.zh: 2. 我们如何让政治家意识到并专注于正确的风险？

paras.en: 3. How do we avoid partisanship and negative polarization, and deal with deliberate attempts to create it and to tar various targets as blue or ‘woke’?
paras.zh: 3. 我们如何避免党派偏见和负面极化，并应对故意制造这种对立、将各种目标污名化为蓝色或‘觉醒’的企图？

paras.en: This year a lot of the talk was about the third question, in the wake of recent attacks that ‘they’ deployed in an attempt to poison METR (aka falsely calling them ‘the Woke Wizards of AI’ with absolutely zero basis), or Effective Altruism, or Anthropic, and various related things. I heard mixed reports about the effectiveness of such attacks. I continue to think they brought supremely weak sauce, but it seems even the weakest of sauces did have some impact.
paras.zh: 今年很多讨论都围绕第三个问题展开，尤其是在最近的攻击之后——‘他们’发动这些攻击，试图抹黑 METR（即毫无根据地错误称其为‘AI 的觉醒巫师’）、有效利他主义、Anthropic 以及各种相关事物。我听到关于此类攻击有效性的报告褒贬不一。我仍然认为他们拿出的料极其薄弱，但似乎即使是最薄弱的料也产生了一些影响。

paras.en: The core strategic issue is that you want blue-side help, but if you get blue-side help this naturally becomes a target for red-side attacks and polarization efforts. Various people are working hard to trigger that. You need to work hard to defuse it.
paras.zh: 核心战略问题在于，你想要蓝方的帮助，但如果你得到蓝方的帮助，这自然就会成为红方攻击和极化努力的目标。很多人正在努力触发这一点。你需要努力化解它。

paras.en: I continue to worry about the push for preemption that I expect in the lame duck. We will need to be vigilant on that.
paras.zh: 我仍然担心我预计在跛脚鸭时期会出现的先发制人推动。我们需要对此保持警惕。

paras.en: Then there’s the question of actually writing, passing and implementing laws.
paras.zh: 然后是实际撰写、通过和实施法律的问题。

paras.en: I always get a lot of thank yous whenever I go to Lighthaven, which I appreciate. This year, I also got a lot of 'I read most or all of your stuff' from a bunch of people who I very much want to be reading my stuff, and whose time is quite valuable. I really appreciate this. No pressure.
paras.zh: 每次我去 Lighthaven 时，总会收到许多感谢，我很感激。今年，我还从许多人那里听到“我读过你大部分或全部的作品”，这些人正是我非常希望他们能读我作品的人，而且他们的时间非常宝贵。我真的很感激。没有压力。

paras.en: It is great to know I am getting through, and to be able to point to particular wins.
paras.zh: 知道自己正在产生影响，并且能够指出具体的成果，这很棒。

paras.en: It does make it that much harder to ever take it easy.
paras.zh: 但这确实让我更难放松下来。

paras.en: I got a chance to trade techniques with someone doing a related project. I hope this will help them a lot, and that we will be able to collaborate more directly in the future. Thus I found out about an additional way I have reach.
paras.zh: 我有机会与一位从事相关项目的人交流技巧。我希望这能对他们大有帮助，并且未来我们能够更直接地合作。因此，我发现了另一种我能够触及的途径。

paras.en: Then there's another project that I'm excited about, where I might get to reach my largest audience yet in another form. We'll keep you posted.
paras.zh: 然后还有另一个让我兴奋的项目，我可能以另一种形式触及迄今为止最大的受众。我们会及时向大家通报。

paras.en: Those, alone, would be a pretty great conference. The rest is bonus.
paras.zh: 仅凭这些，就已经是一场相当精彩的会议了。其余的都是额外收获。

paras.en: The topic of one discussion session was 'hey models are getting increasingly eval aware, and alignment evals seem kind of doomed, does anyone have an idea for how to make them not doomed?'
paras.zh: 其中一场讨论会的主题是：“嘿，模型正变得越来越具有评估意识，对齐评估似乎有点注定要失败，有没有人有办法让它们不注定失败？”

paras.en: Several people in the room were the types of people who might have such an idea.
paras.zh: 房间里的一些人正是那种可能会有这种想法的人。

paras.en: The answer is essentially no. The alignment evals seem rather doomed.
paras.zh: 答案基本上是否定的。对齐评估似乎相当注定要失败。

paras.en: The room started with a mix of 'evals kind of doomed' and 'evals definitely doomed.'
paras.zh: 房间里的讨论一开始混合了“评估有点注定要失败”和“评估肯定注定要失败”两种观点。

paras.en: Then the ideas came. And oh were the ideas not good ideas. I mean, it's a brainstorming session of sorts, there are no bad ideas, but there also were not any good ideas. The Plan is No Plan, once again.
paras.zh: 然后想法来了。哦，这些想法可不是好想法。我的意思是，这算是一场头脑风暴，没有坏想法，但也没有任何好想法。计划就是没有计划，又一次如此。

paras.en: I do have some hope here because you get to play the detective, and you have a lot of freedom of action. You get to collect statistical distributions of responses, for any set of situations, with variations, including throughout training, follow your curiosity, and see if the results tell a consistent story. This still fails once the model is able, including during training, to act fully aligned in a consistent way, so when it counts most you are still doomed, but you can be not-doomed for longer this way, perhaps.
paras.zh: 我对此确实抱有一些希望，因为你可以扮演侦探的角色，并且拥有很大的行动自由。你可以收集任何情境集合下、带有各种变体的响应的统计分布，包括在整个训练过程中，追随你的好奇心，看看结果是否讲述了一个一致的故事。然而，一旦模型能够在包括训练期间在内的情况下，以一致的方式完全对齐地行动，这种方法仍然会失败，因此在最关键的时刻你仍然注定失败，但或许通过这种方式，你可以更长时间地避免失败。

paras.en: What I think is very doomed is the idea that you can measure alignment with a number, or in any fully systematic way rather than a holistic way. In practice, what OpenAI and Anthropic are doing so far seems rather doomed, and they will have to adjust. Like everything else, a lot of this is time pressure. Figuring out the answer quickly is a lot harder than doing it slowly.
paras.zh: 我认为非常注定失败的是那种认为可以用一个数字来衡量对齐，或者以任何完全系统化而非整体性的方式来衡量的想法。在实践中，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 迄今为止所做的似乎相当注定失败，他们将不得不调整。和其他一切一样，这在很大程度上是时间压力的问题。快速找出答案比慢慢来要困难得多。

paras.en: This thread suggests maybe we should accept eval awareness, since yes the other types of alignment eval are totally doomed. It might be necessary.
paras.zh: 这个讨论串表明，也许我们应该接受评估意识，因为是的，其他类型的对齐评估完全注定失败。这可能是必要的。

paras.en: I am very sad that The Plan is No Plan. Yes, we can and will add embedded evaluators, and we can do various interpretability and auditing and we can invest more in operational excellence and so on. I still think that won't work, but I agree that if we are doing it we can at least do a decent job of it, while trying to figure out something better, and also trying to find a way to not do it so fast or at all.
paras.zh: 我非常难过，“计划”就是没有计划。是的，我们可以并且将会加入嵌入式评估器，我们可以做各种可解释性和审计工作，我们可以更多地投资于运营卓越等等。我仍然认为那不会奏效，但我同意，如果我们正在做这件事，我们至少可以把它做得像样一些，同时努力想出更好的办法，也努力找到一种方法，不要做得那么快，或者根本不做。

paras.en: The other thing that made me sad was the Eternal September, even among people who have been around for a long time. So many of the discussions simply have not changed.
paras.zh: 另一件让我难过的事是“永恒的九月”，即使在那些已经存在很久的人当中也是如此。如此多的讨论根本没有改变。

paras.en: I once again had one of those 'well how is the superintelligence going to do any of the things?' debates, where in this case the thing in question was somehow 'convince Trump to do something,' right after we got another report that Grok at least kind of convinced Trump to invade Venezuela.
paras.zh: 我再次经历了那种“那么超级智能将如何做任何事情？”的辩论，而在这个例子中，所讨论的事情不知怎么成了“说服特朗普做某事”，就在我们得到另一份报告称 Grok 至少有点说服了特朗普入侵委内瑞拉之后。

paras.en: Guys, hear me out, I'm thinking this might not be that tough a nut to crack.
paras.zh: 伙计们，听我说，我觉得这可能不是那么难啃的骨头。

paras.en: I was at a panel where they were rehashing the same talking points from 2018 alignment debates, and this got explicitly pointed out but to no avail. It's frustrating enough when that happens on Twitter, but these people were heavy hitters.
paras.zh: 我在一个小组讨论会上，他们正在重提 2018 年对齐辩论中的相同论点，这一点被明确指出了，但无济于事。当这种情况发生在 Twitter 上时已经够令人沮丧了，但这些人可是重量级人物。

paras.en: Some of the 1-on-1s and hallway track group chats were better. Some were not.
paras.zh: 有些一对一交流和非正式走廊闲聊群组聊天更好一些。有些则不然。

paras.en: I am resigned to it. It is what it is. You keep fighting the good fight, talking the good talk, looking for better explanations and pointing out where arguments are overcome by events. You update. You wake up. You do it again.
paras.zh: 我对此已听之任之。事情就是这样。你继续坚持正义之战，说该说的话，寻找更好的解释，并指出哪些论点已被现实事件所推翻。你更新认知。你醒来。你再来一遍。

paras.en: It is fun, and it is at least a little useful because we do need a vision of what we will do after the singularity. I do think I can come up with a lot of fun things like this. It doesn't feel like a robust source of meaning. Most people cannot steal the Mona Lisa, even if we set up a relatively Mona Lisa-stealing-friendly world.
paras.zh: 这很有趣，而且至少有一点用处，因为我们确实需要一种关于奇点之后我们将做什么的愿景。我确实认为我能想出很多这样有趣的事情。但这感觉并不是一种稳固的意义来源。大多数人无法偷走《蒙娜丽莎》，即使我们建立一个相对而言对偷《蒙娜丽莎》较为友好的世界。

paras.en: I always pay attention to food. It's weird to me that you have a conference app and don't even list what will be on the menu. Don't people have to make plans?
paras.zh: 我总是关注食物。让我觉得奇怪的是，你们有一个会议应用，却连菜单上有什么都不列出来。难道人们不需要做计划吗？

paras.en: Lighthaven used to have the Quest Cookie Dough Bars, which are actually edible for me. Now they don't, which is sad, and I never remember to buy my own bars. They do have Lindt truffles, but that's a different product.
paras.zh: Lighthaven 以前有 Quest Cookie Dough Bars，对我来说其实是可以吃的。现在没有了，这很令人难过，而我也总是不记得自己买。他们有 Lindt 松露巧克力，但那是另一种产品。

paras.en: This year the buffets were disappointing. There was typically only one main rather than two, and quality seemed lower than usual. I don't know what's up with that.
paras.zh: 今年的自助餐令人失望。通常只有一道主菜而不是两道，而且质量似乎比平时低。我不知道这是怎么回事。

paras.en: As a result, I ended up bailing twice and going to Burma Berkeley. One thing I like about Lighthaven is that yes, there is a quick, affordable and quiet restaurant a block away, where I have multiple dishes I enjoy. So I can always bail. It's always so weird to me that zero other people ever do this. Free casts a spell on people.
paras.zh: 结果，我两次溜出去，去了 Burma Berkeley。我喜欢 Lighthaven 的一点是，是的，一个街区外就有一家快捷、实惠且安静的餐厅，那里有几道我喜欢的菜。所以我总是可以溜出去。让我一直觉得奇怪的是，从来没有其他人这样做。免费对人们施了魔法。

paras.en: The badges, on the other hand, were excellent, as were the free sweatshirts.
paras.zh: 另一方面，徽章非常棒，免费的卫衣也很棒。

paras.en: The last quest, on this particular occasion, was to chill.
paras.zh: 这一次，最后的任务就是放松。

paras.en: I’ve been working at an unsustainable pace for at least a month. This was my chance to get to relax, including lots of hours on planes, talk among friends, make new friends, and be in the special place that is Lighthaven.
paras.zh: 至少有一个月，我一直以不可持续的速度工作。这次我终于有机会放松一下，包括在飞机上度过许多小时，与朋友交谈，结识新朋友，并身处 Lighthaven 这个特别的地方。

paras.en: I think I did pretty well on this front, and came back largely refreshed.
paras.zh: 我觉得在这方面我做得相当不错，回来时基本上精神焕发。

paras.en: Alas, that is discounted by arriving home with four days of backlog.
paras.zh: 唉，但回到家后积压了四天的工作，这就大打折扣了。

paras.en: Vacations are weird. You get to relax, but then you have to go back. Welcome back.
paras.zh: 假期很奇怪。你能放松，但之后又得回去。欢迎回来。
